data.description:
## Context / Problem
Story `freakish-verminous-agouti` (4cee-8734-7816-4e4c) consolidated the outbound-comment
fit/dedup-key derivation into `fit_for_send(...) -> FittedComment(landed_text, wire_body)` in
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py`, and closed with all seven of its own
acceptance criteria verified and mutation-checked. Those criteria are behavioural, and none of
them claims a construct-uniqueness guard — so the ticket closed honestly.

The gap is against the PARENT EPIC's AC1, not against 4cee's own plan. Epic
`airborne-wellloved-kingfisher` (2ddd-b523-06da-4b4a) requires: "Every duplicated computation
inventoried in the review has exactly one implementation on `main`, each delivered by one
consolidation child; checked by that child's construct-uniqueness test passing in the default
`Verified` tier." An audit of the merged consolidation children found scanning guards for 6f18
(`tests/unit/store/test_store_paths.py`), 1cf6 (`tests/unit/store/test_stamped_lock.py`), 7931
(`tests/unit/test_single_definition_helpers.py`), 25b4
(`tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py`) and 7e0d
(`tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py`), and guards in flight for 4329 and 111a
(Gerrit 2083 and 2082). `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fit_for_send.py` has no scan of
`src/rebar` at all — its only `read_text` is loading a JSON corpus payload.

This matters because the comment key/send fit was one of the WORST offenders in the defect
review that motivated the epic: five copies, arriving as repeated instalments. The
consolidation is real but currently undefended — a sixth copy can merge with nothing failing.

## Approach
Add a construct-uniqueness guard for the fit/dedup-key derivation, built to the epic's rule:
1. Scan every file under `src/rebar` EXCEPT the owner `outbound_comments.py`.
2. Match the CONJUNCTION of atoms that constitute the construct — the fit call together with
   the marker-stripped decode that produces the dedup key — never a single common token such
   as `to_wire(` or `body`, which appear all over the reconciler and would make the guard fire
   on innocent code.
3. Provide a `# comment-fit-ok: <reason>` escape marker whose reason is MANDATORY.
4. Prove teeth by mutation, three ways: an unmarked second derivation FAILS, the same with a
   reasoned marker PASSES, the same with a bare reasonless marker FAILS again.

Derive the exact atom conjunction by reading the landed `fit_for_send` and the two enactment
consumers (`dispatch_one.py`, `dispatch_apply_phases.py`) before writing the matcher.

## Scope
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fit_for_send.py` (or a sibling guard module). No production
change is expected; if the guard finds a genuine second copy, that copy is rewired and the
finding recorded here.

## Testing
The guard itself plus the mutation evidence above. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` passes
unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A test scans every file under `src/rebar` except `outbound_comments.py` and asserts no
      second fit/dedup-key derivation exists; checked by running it.
- [ ] The matcher uses a conjunction of atoms, not a single common token; checked by reading
      the test and by confirming it does not fire on the existing reconciler modules.
- [ ] A reasonless `# comment-fit-ok:` marker is rejected; checked by a negative case.
- [ ] Mutation evidence is recorded: unmarked copy FAILS, reasoned marker PASSES, bare marker
      FAILS; checked by a comment on this ticket quoting the three runs.
data.title: Guard the outbound comment fit against a sixth copy
